subject: Survey of which pinned wheels carry a bundled copy of another project, as compiled code, source code or data (BACKLOG #2935, ASVS 15.1.4)
method: The population and the pins are those of the readings snapshot named above.
A wheel tagged none-any was downloaded, its sha256 checked against the lock, and its file list read for compiled files. Nothing was installed or run.

For any other wheel, the pinned Linux x86_64 wheel for CPython 3.14 or abi3, and the Windows amd64 one, were downloaded and hash-checked the same way, and their contents listed. Extension modules were searched as bytes for needed-library names and version strings. A wheel for another platform was not read.
A file list cannot show code linked into an extension, so the pinned source distribution was read as well, hash-checked the same way.
The `pyside6-addons` and `pyside6-essentials` wheels were not fetched. Their answers rest on PyPI project metadata.

The `pyside6` and `shiboken6` wheels were fetched on 2026-10-05, hash-checked against the harness lock, and their contents listed. PyPI offers no source distribution for either, so those two answers rest on the wheel file lists alone.
Where an answer could not be established, it is recorded as not established and the wheel is treated as carrying.
Each answer carries the date it was made. A wheel surveyed again later carries its own date.
The unit is a package, a library tree or a data set of another project, bundled in the wheel in any form. Each `carries` answer is about that unit.

A single module adapted from another project is not that unit. Where the search found one, the wheel's `adapted_modules` records the file, the project the file names and the words in the file that say so. It changes no answer and is owed no route.
Lines copied into a wheel's own module are not counted. Where the word search hit such lines, the hit is recorded as copied lines.
A second release line of the wheel's own project is not another project. `own_release_lines` records it where one was found.
Each wheel's top-level `carries` and `projects` answer for compiled code. Its `source` and `data` entries answer for the other two forms, and `forms_surveyed` dates them.

For source code and data, every wheel named under `files_read` was fetched again on 2026-10-05, its sha256 checked against the recorded hash and the lock, and its file list read. Nothing was installed or run.
What was looked for is given under `search`: the directory names, the top-level rule, the licence rule, the size rule and the word list.

The word search under `search` was run on 2026-10-05 over every wheel named under `files_read`. Every file it hit is recorded under the wheel's `word_hits` as an adapted module, copied lines or prose.

Each hit line was read with the lines around it. The head of each file recorded as an adapted module was opened. Where two platform wheels of one name were read, their hits were the same and are recorded once.
Prose means the words mark no copy: a sentence that uses them in another sense, or the project's own licence header.
Each `project` under `adapted_modules` is what the file says of itself. No file was compared with the project it names.

Data means another project's or body's published tables, held in the wheel as files or as generated modules: a time zone database, a list of root certificates, Unicode tables, a standard's definitions, a server's schema.
This search reads names, sizes and marked text. What it cannot see is listed under `search`, as `cannot_see`.

A search that finds nothing proves nothing unless it can fire. The `control` entry names a wheel known to vendor source, which is not one of the surveyed wheels. The same search was run over it, and `fired_on` names a path for each rule that fired.
The `pyside6-addons` and `pyside6-essentials` wheels were not fetched for this either. Their source and data answers are recorded as not established.

search.directory_rule: A directory at any depth in the wheel whose name, in lower case, is one of `directories`.
search.top_level_rule: A top-level name in the wheel's file list beyond the project's own package, module or compiled file.
search.licence_rule: A file whose path holds `licen`, `notice`, `copying`, `authors`, `credits` or `third`, in any case, and that is named for another project. The names were read by hand.
search.size_rule: A file outside `.dist-info` whose name does not end in `.py` or `.pyi`, and whose size is over 20,000 bytes.
search.module_rule: A `.py` module was opened where its name or its size suggested a generated table. This rule was applied by hand and is not exact.
words: redistribution and use in source and binary forms
search.word_rule: Each file outside `.dist-info` whose name ends in one of `suffixes` was decoded as UTF-8 and put in lower case. Each line was searched for each of `words` as a substring.
cannot_see: A copy that carries none of `words`, sits under no directory in `directories`, and has no licence file named for another project.
A module adapted from another project that says so in other words, or does not say so. So `adapted_modules` lists what was found and is not a full list.
Whether a file matches the project it names. No file was compared with its source.
Text in a file whose name ends in none of `suffixes`, and anything inside a compiled file.
A wheel that was not fetched, or a wheel for another platform.

What a large `.py` module holds, where it was not opened as a possible table. At least these were not opened: each `.py` file over 100 KB in `anyio`, `click`, `fastapi`, `pyasn1`, `pydantic`, `pydantic-core` and `typing-extensions`, and `ldap3/protocol/oid.py`, about 127 KB, which its name suggests is a table of object identifiers. So a `no` under `data` does not rest on every large module having been opened.

control.note: pip vendors its dependencies in source form. The directory rule fired on `pip/_vendor`. The licence rule fired on the files under `licenses/src/pip/_vendor`, each named for a vendored project. The size rule fired on `pip/_vendor/certifi/cacert.pem`, 234,354 bytes. The word `vendored` hit `pip/_vendor/__init__.py`, first at line 26, and the word search hit 35 files of the wheel in all. The top-level rule did not fire, because pip's one top-level name is its own. So that rule has no control here. The sha256 is the one PyPI states for the file. Two locks in this repository pin pip, `uv.lock` and `ci/locks/ci-scanners.lock`, and both pin pip 26.2. The control is pip 26.2.1, a different version. So its hash cannot be checked against a lock in this repository.

wheels.name: pyside6-addons
wheels.evidence: The wheel was not fetched or listed. Its PyPI description says it includes Qt modules, and PyPI lists the Linux wheel at about 175 MB. The Qt version inside was not read, and nothing else the wheel bundles was looked for.
